focus: CI on/off control part 1: vars.* gating, skipped-check semantics, clone/fork defaults
answeredQuestions: What on/off control design lets a clone or base repo disable workflows or groups without editing YAML?

label: No workflow in the repository reads vars.<NAME> and no job-level if: reads an environment value: a sweep of all 33 files in .github/workflows/ returns zero matches for both. Only four job-level if: conditions exist, all event- or needs-driven (dependabot-auto-merge.yml:18, trigger-index-rebuild.yml:33, trigger-index-rebuild.yml:186, skill-doc-frontmatter.yml:52), so the on/off surface is greenfield while the expression idiom is already established.

Any on/off gate must sit at job level, never at trigger level. GitHub's workflow-syntax reference documents that 'If a workflow is skipped due to branch filtering, path filtering, or a commit message, then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a Pending state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful will be blocked from merging.' No context (vars, env, inputs) is available in on.push or on.pull_request filters, so a variable can never prevent a workflow from triggering and can only prevent its jobs from doing work.

The complementary claim that a job skipped by a job-level if: still produces a check-run treated as success by required status checks could NOT be verified this iteration: the GitHub how-to page for conditions returned HTTP 404 and the phrase does not appear in the workflow-syntax reference that was fetched. Labelled inferred; phase 002 must confirm before the job-level gate recommendation is adopted, because if false the recommendation degrades into blocked merges.

.skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env cannot serve as the CI on/off control because it is gitignored (.gitignore:354-355) and therefore absent from a GitHub Actions checkout, where a switch read from it would silently do nothing. What is reusable is its shape: committed example (hook-flags.env.example:1 says copy and uncomment what you want OFF), gitignored local override, everything ON by default, environment wins over file. vars.* reproduces that on GitHub's side because an unset variable resolves to an empty string, so a condition written as vars.X != 'off' stays TRUE and the job runs. A committed .skilled/ci.json is strictly more expensive: a job-level if: cannot read a file, so it needs a checkout-and-parse job plus needs.outputs fan-out in every workflow that wants a switch.

The group taxonomy for the control already exists in documentation: .github/workflows/README.md:60 classifies every workflow into trigger tiers (whole-tree guards, release-lines-only, path-filtered suites, review-time PR-only, Dependabot-only, message-contract, weekly report, rebuild). Five to six tiers is the right granularity; 33 per-workflow switches would be overengineering and would drift on every added workflow with no check able to catch the drift.

vars.* gating reduces billed runner minutes but not workflow-run volume: 28 of 33 workflows declare a push: trigger, and a gated-off workflow still creates a workflow-run record whose jobs skip without allocating a runner. The only zero-run lever is GitHub's repository-level Actions control or editing on: -- and editing on: is both excluded by the angle and the one change that turns required checks Pending. Phase 002 must not promise trigger-level savings from the variable design.

The variable design addresses base repositories and clones, not forks. For a clone the default-on property is structural, not documented: git clone carries the commit graph and no repository settings or variables, so every SKILLED_CI_* resolves empty and every job runs; the clone can only switch things off after it creates its own repository variables. For a fork, a pull_request from the fork executes in the base repository's context, so the base repo's variables apply and a contributor cannot disable CI from their own fork. The clone direction is confirmed by construction; the fork direction is inferred (the GitHub variables page 404'd this iteration).

Every CI on/off condition must evaluate TRUE when its variable is unset, so an untouched clone or base repository runs everything; the only disabling literal is an explicit opt-out value such as 'off', and a gate must never sit in front of a job whose name a branch-protection rule requires unless the skipped-job semantics of f-iter010-003 are confirmed.
No CI control may depend on a gitignored file, because a gitignored file does not exist on a GitHub Actions runner and the switch would fail silently rather than at load time.

direction: Trigger-level gating with vars.* in on.push/on.pull_request filters
reason: No context is available in trigger filters, so the expression cannot be written at all; and even if it could, a workflow skipped by a filter leaves required checks Pending and blocks merges (documented).

direction: Reusing .skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env as the CI switch file
reason: The file is gitignored (.gitignore:354-355) and therefore absent from every CI checkout; a switch read from it would silently do nothing on the runner.

direction: A committed .skilled/ci.json as the primary on/off mechanism
reason: A job-level if: cannot read a file, so it requires a checkout-and-parse gate job plus needs.outputs fan-out in every workflow that wants a switch -- more runner cost than the minutes it saves, versus vars.* which needs no job and no checkout.
